HEADLINE: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections

CORE FACTS
- Obama campaigned on Saturday in BOTH Ohio and Michigan. This resolves an apparent conflict: Al Jazeera's cached file reports an Ohio rally, the Guardian's index reports a Michigan crowd. He did both; they are not competing accounts.
- The midterm elections are on 3 November and will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's term.
- Early voting has already begun. Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in West Palm Beach, Florida, alongside First Lady Melania Trump, before going to support Republican candidate Mike Collins in Georgia.
- Obama's Ohio rally supported ex-Senator Sherrod Brown, running to unseat incumbent Republican Senator John Husted, and Amy Acton, running for state governor against Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.
- Trump held a rally in Perry, Georgia.

OBAMA, NAMED QUOTES, FORMER PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES
- "This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration" — told crowds in Ohio on Saturday.
- In Cleveland: "After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, 'enough is enough'."
- On the economy, referring to Trump without naming him: "If you thought everything was too expensive before 'you know who', everything is more expensive now."
- THE MOST NEWSWORTHY LINE, and the one that connects to the Hormuz through-line: in Ohio, Obama told Democrat supporters the Iran conflict had given Tehran "veto power" over the Strait of Hormuz.
- On the White House renovation: "What's with all the gold? He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened up a Cheesecake Factory."
- On Ramaswamy's attack advert featuring Acton's estranged mother: "In recent days, we've seen there is no line he will not cross. No low he will not sink to try to get in the limelight. I mean, think about this latest ad he ran." The BBC notes the advert did not mention that the woman's husband was charged with raping Acton when she was a child.
- Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic, but said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy.

TRUMP, NAMED QUOTES, PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES
- At the Georgia rally: "we're in the golden age of America".
- On oil, acknowledging prices were "temporarily high": "our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down". The BBC notes fuel prices have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
- "we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs", and he repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress.
- Of the Democrats: they would "loot your wealth" and "annihilate your borders". He accused them of trying to open up immigration from Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia, which he described as "terror-infested".
- ON IRAN, ASKED EARLIER IN THE DAY — THIS IS THE VERBATIM TEXT BEHIND THE "IMMINENT STRIKE" FRAMING: "I've done it very effectively and I may have to finish it off, or maybe they'll make a deal, but I'm not sure. Either way, we win."
- Asked whether Melania Trump would visit Ukraine after the White House announced she secured a ceasefire in a Russian-occupied city: "We will see."
- Amy Acton spoke at the rally before Obama, arguing Ramaswamy "has chosen to exploit my childhood" to "save his struggling campaign".

ASSESSMENT: this is more than a stump speech. The Hormuz "veto power" line is a former president accusing the sitting administration of handing Iran leverage over a global chokepoint, delivered nine days before the midterms, and it is a substantive foreign-policy charge rather than a rhetorical flourish.
